prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2253 is the root-cause fix: it spans both streamable_http.py (terminate() now iterates and closes every registered SSE writer generically) and streamable_http_manager.py (the lifespan shutdown path now calls terminate() on all active sessions before cancelling tasks, which is the actual trigger needed on manager shutdown). #3218 only touches streamable_http.py and adds registration of the GET/standalone stream writer into that same dict; its own inline comment ('so that session terminate() can close this ASGI response') shows it is written to depend on the closing loop #2253 adds, and it never adds the manager-level shutdown-triggering change its own title claims to fix. prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs touch the same line in stdio_server() that creates the write_stream memory object stream, instantiated with buffer size 0. prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same root cause: `_request_streams` is keyed by request id, so two concurrent requests that map to the same key silently overwrite each other's routing slot, cross-wiring or hanging responses. #3063 adds a simple `if request_id in self._request_streams` guard using `str(message.id)` as the key. #3221 implements the identical guard but replaces the key derivation with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) so integer id `1` and string id `"1"` aren't collapsed into the same key, and so a string id equal to `GET_STREAM_KEY` (`"_GET_stream"`) can't collide with the standalone GET stream slot — both are collision scenarios `str(message.id)` alone does not cover. (2 PRs)

prs.author: draesthetic

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: All three fix the same bug: pickling an MCPError (especially UrlElicitationRequiredError) fails because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ calls cls(*self.args), and self.args (set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__) doesn't match subclass constructor signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) — raising a TypeError on unpickle. This is issue #2431, explicitly referenced by #2555 and matched by #3262's identical title; #2478 frames it more broadly as 'preserve payload on pickle' but touches the same __reduce__/reconstruction path in the same file region. (3 PRs)

This is issue #2431, explicitly referenced by #2555 and matched by #3262's identical title; #2478 frames it more broadly as 'preserve payload on pickle' but touches the same __reduce__/reconstruction path in the same file region. prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ on the base MCPError class itself, using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__ to rebuild the instance and restoring the full __dict__ as pickle state — this covers every current and future MCPError subclass without per-subclass logic, and its test diff extends coverage to NoBackChannelError (not just UrlElicitationRequiredError) to demonstrate that generality. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from (elicitations, message) alone, which drops any other instance state and leaves every other MCPError subclass with the same unpickle bug. 2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes an 'if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' branch dispatching to from_error vs from_error_data — functionally similar in scope to 3262 but requires manually extending that if/else for any future subclass with a divergent constructor, whereas 3262's __new__/__dict__ approach needs no per-class maintenance.

members.author: yaowubarbara

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ on the base MCPError class itself, using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__ to rebuild the instance and restoring the full __dict__ as pickle state — this covers every current and future MCPError subclass without per-subclass logic, and its test diff extends coverage to NoBackChannelError (not just UrlElicitationRequiredError) to demonstrate that generality. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from (elicitations, message) alone, which drops any other instance state and leaves every other MCPError subclass with the same unpickle bug. 2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes an 'if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' branch dispatching to from_error vs from_error_data — functionally similar in scope to 3262 but requires manually extending that if/else for any future subclass with a divergent constructor, whereas 3262's __new__/__dict__ approach needs no per-class maintenance.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Both fix the same root cause: `_request_streams` is keyed by request id, so two concurrent requests that map to the same key silently overwrite each other's routing slot, cross-wiring or hanging responses. #3063 adds a simple `if request_id in self._request_streams` guard using `str(message.id)` as the key. #3221 implements the identical guard but replaces the key derivation with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) so integer id `1` and string id `"1"` aren't collapsed into the same key, and so a string id equal to `GET_STREAM_KEY` (`"_GET_stream"`) can't collide with the standalone GET stream slot — both are collision scenarios `str(message.id)` alone does not cover.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ on the base MCPError class itself, using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__ to rebuild the instance and restoring the full __dict__ as pickle state — this covers every current and future MCPError subclass without per-subclass logic, and its test diff extends coverage to NoBackChannelError (not just UrlElicitationRequiredError) to demonstrate that generality. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from (elicitations, message) alone, which drops any other instance state and leaves every other MCPError subclass with the same unpickle bug. 2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes an 'if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' branch dispatching to from_error vs from_error_data — functionally similar in scope to 3262 but requires manually extending that if/else for any future subclass with a divergent constructor, whereas 3262's __new__/__dict__ approach needs no per-class maintenance.

clusters.pick_reason: 3243 is the only one of the three that changes context.lock's type from anyio.Lock to a task-agnostic anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) — needed because httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different anyio task than the one that acquired the lock — and it adds a separate flow_lock so refresh/authorization transitions single-flight independently of normal per-request token attachment. 2858 (a rebase of the older community PR #2660) and 3252 both only relocate a single `async with self.context.lock:` block around the same anyio.Lock, without addressing the cross-task acquire/release case or separating the two critical sections.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Both fix the same root cause: `_request_streams` is keyed by request id, so two concurrent requests that map to the same key silently overwrite each other's routing slot, cross-wiring or hanging responses. #3063 adds a simple `if request_id in self._request_streams` guard using `str(message.id)` as the key. #3221 implements the identical guard but replaces the key derivation with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) so integer id `1` and string id `"1"` aren't collapsed into the same key, and so a string id equal to `GET_STREAM_KEY` (`"_GET_stream"`) can't collide with the standalone GET stream slot — both are collision scenarios `str(message.id)` alone does not cover.
